subject: Dedicated reserved pool — surge guardrails & sizing proposal (Solaris Tech)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morales <alex.morales@solaristech.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@solaristech.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated reserved pool — surge guardrails & sizing proposal (draft)

Hi Alex — thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation attached is a concise proposal for the Dedicated (reserved) pool sizing and the operational guardrails we recommend for Solaris Tech while you ramp. High-level items below; full numbers in the attached Solaris_capacity_plan_v3.xlsx.

Summary proposal (draft):
- Reserved baseline: 12 H100 nodes (16 x 80GB H100 GPUs equivalent) sized to support steady-state peak inference for your reported 400k tokens/min workload.
- Guaranteed throughput: baseline SLA of 99.9% availability at baseline capacity.
- Short-term surge/burst model:
  - Controlled burst headroom: allow up to 2.0x sustained throughput for up to 15 minutes, refreshed on a rolling window.
  - Spike acceleration: allow up to 4.0x instantaneous acceleration for up to 90 seconds (fast-path burst) before throttling to 2.0x.
  - Burst budget: accumulate 1% of baseline capacity per hour (up to 48% of baseline) as "burst credits" for unexpected spikes.
- Autoscale behavior: automatic horizontal burst across reserved pool with priority routing; if burst budget is exhausted, requests will be routed to compatible lower-cost model variants (same family, quantized) or to hosted failover region per your preference.
- Billing during burst: default model charges burst at 2x unit compute rate after a 10-minute daily free grace; we can convert to committed burst minutes at a predictable blended rate if you prefer contract-side caps.

Action items for Solaris:
1) Confirm whether a 10-minute daily free grace is acceptable to procurement.
2) Indicate if you want burst billing to be capped monthly or converted into a purchased burst bundle.
3) Confirm whether automatic fallback to a quantized model variant is permitted for P1 inference types (latency-sensitive).

Attachments: Solaris_capacity_plan_v3.xlsx (capacity math, node counts, model variant mapping).

If that looks reasonable I'll draft a short SLA addendum to append to the Reserved Capacity Agreement and include the DocuSign link for signature.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa — thanks for sending this over and for the clear math in the sheet. A few quick clarifying questions from procurement and finance before we escalate to legal:

1) Billing during bursts — can you clarify how the 2x unit compute rate applies to partial-minute bursts and to the 90s spike window? Will we be billed per-second granularity or rounded to the nearest minute?
2) Fallback behavior — if requests are routed to a quantized variant, what visibility/metric will we get showing quality deltas (latency/response degradation) so we can track user-impact?
3) Preemption & priority — will Solaris traffic be preempted in a cross-customer outage, or does reserved capacity guarantee the baseline slices are never re-allocated?

Procurement also asked for the SLA addendum draft and a line-item showing the opt-in contracted burst bundle (e.g., 50k burst-minutes/month at a fixed rate). Can you send a draft SLA addendum and a sample purchase order line?

Folks — looping you in for a quick triage. Solaris asked the procurement/finance questions below. Need firm guidance on: billing granularity for bursts, acceptable default fallback policy, and whether infra will allow stronger allocation assurances for baseline.

Questions from Solaris (copied):
- Bill granularity for bursts (per-second vs per-minute and rounding rules).
- Visibility for quality deltas when falling back to quantized model variants.
- Guarantee that baseline reserved slices won't be preempted.

My suggested immediate responses:
1) Billing granularity: we bill bursts at per-minute granularity with per-second metering; partial minutes are pro-rated but shown rounded in invoice lines to nearest second for transparency. For the 90s spike, we meter at second granularity and apply the burst multiplier to consumed compute seconds. (Need Marissa to confirm accounting/billing systems can surface this exactly.)
2) Visibility/metrics: Sales Eng (Karthik) and Infra (Marcus) to confirm we can surface a per-request quality delta (latency + default LLM score drop) and tie it to the rollback timeline; suggest exposing this via the Console per-route delta metric and an automatic tag on requests served by fallback models.
3) Preemption: baseline reserved slices are non-preemptible. Burst expansion uses elastic headroom pool that may temporarily borrow capacity from shared regions under extreme global stress; in that rare case, priority will be Solaris -> other hosted customers, but we can add a contractual clause that we will not preempt below baseline except for force majeure. (Marcus please confirm viability.)

Also, procurement requested a sample contracted burst bundle (pre-purchased minutes) — Marissa, can you produce a 3-tier sample (Small/Medium/Large) with price-per-minute and a blended overage rate? We should also draft an SLA addendum with a 10-minute daily free grace, the burst bucket accounting, and the billing multiplier/default fallback rules.

I tried to keep the language conservative; want to get internal alignment before sending to Alex/CFO.

Thanks —
Vanessa

Vanessa — thanks for the clear ask. Quick alignment below; this is the language I recommend we send to Solaris with the SLA addendum draft attached.

Internal decisions / consensus:
- Billing granularity: Finance confirms we can present per-second metering; invoice lines will show per-minute aggregation but charges are pro-rated to the second (rounding only for display). We'll state "metered per-second, invoiced per-minute with per-second pro-ration" in the addendum.
- Burst billing model: keep the proposed 2x multiplier after a 10-minute daily free grace. Offer an opt-in contracted burst bundle (example tiers attached) at a ~1.6x blended rate for pre-purchased minutes to provide predictability.
- Fallback model visibility: Karthik can expose a per-route "fallback delta" metric in the Console that reports (latency delta, sample quality score) for any request served by a fallback variant; we'll include a sample dashboard link in the addendum.
- Baseline non-preemption: Marcus confirms baseline reserved slices are non-preemptible. Elastic headroom is subject to cross-region borrowing only in declared regional capacity emergencies; we agree to a contractual clause limiting preemption below baseline to force majeure only.

Next steps (for the email back to Solaris):
1) Send the SLA_addendum_draft.pdf (attached) and the 3-tier contracted burst bundle pricing spreadsheet (included in the capacity workbook).
2) Offer a one-week review period with procurement; commit Redwood to a technical sync between Karthik and Solaris engineering to calibrate fallback deltas.
3) If Solaris agrees, we prepare a DocuSign envelope for the addendum plus the Reserved Capacity PO (template attached).

I'll attach the SLA_addendum_draft.pdf (included) and a pre-filled DocuSign envelope stub once you approve the language.
